In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aging decreases genomic DNA in mouse colons and increases promoter DNA methylation and expression.
the age-related increase in promoter methylation of p16 in the mouse colon is dependent on dietary folate intake.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aging is a determinant of both genomic DNA methylation, as well as the p16-specific DNA demethylation and reexpression that is a hallmark of colon cancer.
aging is a major determinant of DNA methylation, and dietary folate can modulate DNA methylation in a direction opposite to the effect of aging.
aging and dietary folates are important determinants of genomic as well as p16-specific DNA methylations in mouse colons.
The main takeaway from our work is that

older age and inadequate folates are important determinants of genomic DNA methylation, which is relevant to carcinogenesis, and that these two factors may act synergistically in the colon to enhance carcinogenesis.
aging and folate deficiency are important determinants of DNA methylation patterns and that these changes may play important roles in carcinogenesis.
aging and folate status interactively regulate DNA methylation in a manner that is likely to be relevant to the development of colon cancer.
